title: 3D CNN MRI endophenotype guides discovery of dystonia genes RAP1GAP, TNN and ITSN2
summary: DystoniaGeneNet, a 3D convolutional neural network trained on T1 MRIs of 40 familial laryngeal dystonia patients and 40 controls, classified 85.7% of independent familial cases correctly. Its predictions guided variant prioritization in 214 exomes, with replication in 738 exomes, a biobank (892 cases, 2,475 controls) and All of Us (1,343 cases, 6,840 controls). Rare variants in RAP1GAP and TNN segregated with disease, ITSN2 variants appeared in predicted-familial sporadic cases, and qPCR/RNA-seq (n = 74) showed reduced RAP1GAP and ITSN2 expression in carriers. Small training set; medRxiv preprint.
ai_technology: DystoniaGeneNet 3D convolutional neural network on T1-weighted brain MRI
organization: Broad Institute; Harvard University; Massachusetts General Hospital

evidence.tested: Independent MRI cohorts, replication exomes and biobanks, and expression assays in variant carriers.
evidence.unknown: Causality of the genes and generalization of the small-sample model; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts familial status from MRI to prioritize genetic analyses.
